bug_semantics: On a glamor-backed X server, glamor_font_get() sized a CPU-side font-atlas heap buffer and each glyph slot from the font's declared maxbounds, but copied each bitmap using that glyph's unchecked GLYPHWIDTHBYTES and GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS metrics. libXfont2's PCF parser did not recompute maxbounds from the per-glyph records, so an authenticated X client could supply a PCF whose individual metrics exceeded (or were negative relative to) maxbounds; drawing text then made the row memcpy write attacker-controlled bytes beyond the allocated atlas, with negative values also permitting unsigned/size_t wrap.
flaw_origin: Commit 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f changed glamor_font_get() from issuing one glTexSubImage2D call per glyph to building one CPU heap staging atlas. It introduced bits = malloc(overall_width * overall_height), where overall_width/height came from maxbounds, together with a loop bounded by GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS(glyph) and memcpy(dst, src, GLYPHWIDTHBYTES(glyph)) without checking those per-glyph dimensions against the maxbounds-derived slot. That new mismatch is the exact heap-buffer-overflow mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: the exact commit object for 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f names human author Michel Dänzer <michel.daenzer@amd.com> and human committer Keith Packard <keithp@keithp.com>; its message has only Reviewed-by and Signed-off-by trailers and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI-attribution marker.
evidence: First-party disclosure https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/07/08/2 identifies CVE-2026-55999 as the glamor font-atlas heap overflow, gives the SetFontPath -> OpenFont -> glamor text-draw attack path, limits exposure to glamor-backed Xorg/Xwayland, states fixed boundaries xorg-server-21.1.24 and xwayland-24.1.13, and cites fbf7bac22e2c6bd627fb042742a23318263edae1. In the validated full-history clone, git log -L ':glamor_font_get:glamor/glamor_font.c' at the fix parent and git log -S'memcpy(dst, src, GLYPHWIDTHBYTES(glyph))' trace the vulnerable heap-copy lines to 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f. git show 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f -- glamor/glamor_font.c shows that commit adding the maxbounds-sized malloc plus the unchecked per-glyph memcpy loop. The only other 2015 -S hit, 8415eca0abc00ec96cb94cd656b58edbfa8f09a3, explicitly says it is a later cherry-pick of 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f, so it is not the source BIC. Direct parent-tree inspection with git show ac94cdb9df94dd26688de6d3d9143ac48f7b3c7b:glamor/glamor_font.c shows no bits heap atlas, no malloc for it, and no memcpy loop: it uploads each glyph through glTexSubImage2D, proving the exact heap flaw absent in the immediate parent. git show fbf7bac22e2c6bd627fb042742a23318263edae1 shows the direct fix in glamor/glamor_font.c: reject nonpositive atlas dimensions and reject negative or over-slot per-glyph width/height before copying. Release history contains equivalent direct backports f3df3c9a52b4f480cbcff45cc6569c19de6bfede (git tag --contains: xorg-server-21.1.24) and 28bf4097755f0f9e45e2cfc097e2bb49a714c227 (git tag --contains: xwayland-24.1.13). Tag commits resolve to xorg-server-21.1.23=8570e9fcec845f68f0c90caa51fd7a24764ea220, xorg-server-21.1.24=65d790bd208ec380b196eb98f144abb0b32e334d, xwayland-24.1.12=af4b3d7250366e1a3822919e41fcf66da4966af2, and xwayland-24.1.13=c5a47fda896aeefbf1d06a73e392a294344f9e1a. git merge-base returns the BIC itself against both prior vulnerable tags; it returns each release backport itself against the corresponding patched tag, while the backport/prior-tag merge bases are the prior tag commits rather than the fixes. Finally, git cat-file commit 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f supplies the BIC-only identity/trailer check quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely the older use of per-glyph metrics: the disclosed CWE-122 occurs when a maxbounds-sized CPU heap atlas is populated with unchecked per-glyph-sized copies. History shows the smallest commit that first created that exact allocation/copy mismatch is 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f; its parent used direct GL uploads and therefore lacked the heap buffer and heap memcpy sink. Later layout changes preserved the mismatch, and the 2026 fix added the missing dimensional invariant checks. The BIC is in both last-known vulnerable release tags, while branch-equivalent fixes first appear in the disclosed patched tags, matching the advisory boundary. The cited mainline fix is already a direct one-parent patch, so direct_fix_sha equals fix_sha and no squash decomposition is needed. AI attribution is decided only from the BIC commit object: it has human author/committer identities and no AI marker. Later AI assistance on unrelated or fixing commits cannot attribute this 2015 BIC, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
